full_judgment: 7. However, we find force in the second submission of Mr. Dutta that the impugned judgment is too brief and delivered hastily without observing mandatory provision of the Code of Civil Procedure. There are series of decision of the appellate Division in support of this view. Some of them are 25 DLR (AD) 90, 1 BLD (AD)371 and 45 DLR (AD) 112. In all these decisions it has been held that while passing the judgment even exparte the court is required to comply with the Provisions of order 20, rule 4, C.P.C. which prescribes that the judgments of the courts shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon and the reasons for such decisions. In the impugned judgment we find total absence of these requirements and as such the impugned judgment, we hold, cannot be maintained and must be set aside defendant filed an application on 15.6.88 directing the plaintiff to produce certain documents and the learned sub-ordinate Judge illegally rejected the said application. We allow the defendant be file such an application afresh and the learned sub-ordinate Judge is directed to allow the same. However, it will be the plaintiffs option either to produce or not to produce the documents and if those documents were not produced the court shall consider whether to take adverse presumption in terms of section 1 14(g) of the Evidence Act.
